# qwen-image — prompting & settings guide

- **Prompting style:** natural_language
- **Negative prompt:** supported
- **Prompt weights** (e.g. `(word:1.2)`): not honored
- **Loader:** UNETLoader + CLIPLoader

## Recommended settings

| steps | cfg | sampler | scheduler | resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 20 | 2.5 | euler | simple | 1328x1328 |

## Tips

- Qwen-Image excels at long, detailed natural-language prompts and accurate text rendering (including Chinese).
- It supports a real negative prompt and true CFG — a low cfg (~2.5-4) keeps it stable.
- Lightning/distilled Qwen variants run at 4-8 steps with cfg 1.0 — match settings to the variant.

## Common mistakes

- Don't assume it ignores negatives like Flux — Qwen-Image does honor a negative prompt.
- Don't push cfg to 7+; Qwen-Image prefers a low CFG and oversaturates at high values.

## Example prompt

> A storefront sign that reads "福满楼" in elegant gold calligraphy above a bustling night market, lanterns glowing, crowd in soft focus, photorealistic.

MiniMax H3 is audio-native: voice, sound effects and music are generated with the picture in a single pass, so describe the sound in the same prompt as the shots and camera moves.
State the whole scene first (location, character, what is happening), then break it into timed shots — an explicit [0s-2s] / [2s-5s] timeline steers both the cuts and the audio.

h3.raw:
# minimax-h3 — prompting & settings guide

- **Prompting style:** natural_language
- **Negative prompt:** ignored — do not pass one
- **Prompt weights** (e.g. `(word:1.2)`): not honored
- **Loader:** UNETLoader + CLIPLoader (type minimax) + two VAELoaders (video VAE + audio VAE)

## Recommended settings

| steps | cfg | sampler | scheduler | resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 20 | 1 | res_multistep | simple | 1344x768 |

## Tips

- MiniMax H3 is audio-native: voice, sound effects and music are generated with the picture in a single pass, so describe the sound in the same prompt as the shots and camera moves.
- State the whole scene first (location, character, what is happening), then break it into timed shots — an explicit [0s-2s] / [2s-5s] timeline steers both the cuts and the audio.
- Native canvas is a 768px short edge — 1344x768 at 16:9 — rounded to a multiple of 32; the shipped templates open at a smaller fast-preview size, so raise it for final output. Duration snaps to H3's 17-frames-per-block (17k+5) grid at 24fps.
- 20 steps is the template default; ~25 buys better motion quality. The H3 nodes take a single prompt and emit one conditioning, and the templates sample through a guidance-free BasicGuider, so there is no cfg dial or negative-prompt input to reach for — steer with the prompt alone.
- To go faster, first flip the shipped video_minimax_h3_* template's Boolean (Enable Lightning LoRA) switch (default off): it swaps in the 8-step turbo LoRA minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_8step_v1.0_comfyui_bf16 (R2V: minimax_h3_ref2v_turbo_4step_v0.1_comfyui_bf16, which runs at 4) and drops steps to 6 (R2V: 4) with the built-in 12/3 shift, at the cost of slightly weaker audio and motion; the 8-step LoRA itself runs at 8 steps outside the template. Only if that is still too slow: (2) the FastVideo FastH3 8-step checkpoint via the video_fastvideo_fasth3_t2v / video_fastvideo_fasth3_i2v templates (a separate 8-step distilled checkpoint, fastvideo_fasth3_8step_v2_pruned_int8_convrot, with its shift pre-wired at 10/3; T2V and I2V only); (3) the 768p 4-step LoRA minimax_h3_fl2v_turbo_4step_v1.0_768p at 4 steps, which needs an explicit MiniMaxH3SigmaShift at 6/3; (4) fewer pixels or a shorter duration (generation time grows superlinearly with pixel count). The paid api_minimax_h3_max_turbo_t2v / _i2v templates (run_template) are the fastest route (768p in ~1-3 s) but cost partner fees, so offer them as a route change rather than picking them silently.
- Sigma shift is a real dial, set with a MiniMaxH3SigmaShift node between the model loader and the guider. Its defaults (shift_video 12, shift_audio 3) are what the base model and the 8-step turbo LoRA expect; the 768p 4-step turbo variant (rung 3 above) was distilled at 6/3, so set them explicitly for that one. The video_minimax_h3_* templates omit the node and run the built-in 12/3; the FastH3 templates pre-wire it at 10/3.
- Reference each R2V input by tag in connection order (<Picture 1>, <Video 1>, <Audio 1>) and say which reference drives identity, style, motion, camera or voice — explicit assignments work much better than leaving it implied.

## Common mistakes

- Don't run the base checkpoint at the turbo LoRA's 4-8 steps — without a Lightning LoRA loaded, H3 wants its full ~20-25 steps.
- Don't run a turbo LoRA at the base 20-25 steps either — the 8-step and 4-step distillations are trained for those step counts and extra steps only burn GPU time.
- Don't cross the turbo LoRAs over, and don't carry one variant's shift over to another: the fl2v turbo LoRA belongs on the fl2va (T2V/I2V) model and the ref2v turbo LoRA on the ref2va (R2V) model.
- Don't budget prompt tokens for a negative prompt or hunt for a cfg dial — the H3 nodes expose a single prompt input and the templates guide with BasicGuider; put the steering in the prompt instead.
- Don't answer 'make it faster' with the whole turbo menu — the template's Lightning switch is the default; the other rungs are for when it is not enough.
- Don't treat it as a silent video model: the workflow decodes a second, audio VAE and muxes stereo audio into the MP4, so a prompt with no sound direction throws away half the model.

## Example prompt

> A rain-slicked Tokyo alley at dusk, neon signs humming, steam drifting off a ramen cart. [0s-3s] The camera pushes slowly past the cart as the chef slides a bowl across the counter — ceramic clinks, broth bubbles, rain patters on the awning. [3s-6s] A cyclist rings a bell and glides through frame, tyres hissing on wet asphalt, distant city hum under a soft synth pad.

sdxl.raw:
# sdxl — prompting & settings guide

- **Prompting style:** hybrid
- **Negative prompt:** supported
- **Prompt weights** (e.g. `(word:1.2)`): supported
- **Loader:** CheckpointLoaderSimple

## Recommended settings

| steps | cfg | sampler | scheduler | resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 30 | 7 | dpmpp_2m | karras | 1024x1024 |

## Tips

- SDXL works well with both descriptive phrases and comma-separated tags — quality boosters like "highly detailed, sharp focus" still help.
- Always pair a positive with a negative prompt; a short quality-negative ("blurry, lowres, jpeg artifacts, watermark") noticeably cleans output.
- Generate at 1024x1024 (or an SDXL-native aspect like 832x1216); 512x512 produces poor anatomy on SDXL.
- Prompt weights like (word:1.2) are honored — use them sparingly to emphasize.

## Common mistakes

- Don't generate at 512x512 — SDXL is trained for ~1MP and falls apart at SD1.5 resolutions.
- Don't drop the negative prompt — SDXL relies on real CFG and benefits from one.
- Anime/booru checkpoints (Pony, Illustrious, NoobAI) want booru tags + their score/quality tags, not prose.

## Example prompt

> A majestic snow leopard perched on a rocky ledge, intricate fur detail, mountain backdrop, golden hour light, highly detailed, sharp focus, 8k. Negative: blurry, lowres, jpeg artifacts, watermark.

# flux-dev — prompting & settings guide

- **Prompting style:** natural_language
- **Negative prompt:** ignored — do not pass one
- **Prompt weights** (e.g. `(word:1.2)`): not honored
- **Loader:** UNETLoader + DualCLIPLoader

## Recommended settings

| steps | cfg | sampler | scheduler | resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 20 | 1 | euler | simple | 1024x1024 |

## Tips

- Write rich, descriptive natural-language sentences; Flux follows long prose prompts well.
- Keep the KSampler cfg at 1.0 and steer prompt adherence with a FluxGuidance node (≈3.5) instead.
- 20 steps is a good default; 25-30 only for fine detail.

## Common mistakes

- Don't pass a negative prompt — Flux ignores CFG>1 / negatives; raising KSampler cfg above 1 degrades output.
- Don't use prompt weights like (word:1.3) — Flux's T5 text encoder does not honor them.
- Don't load it through CheckpointLoaderSimple — Flux ships as a diffusion_model + separate CLIP (UNETLoader + DualCLIPLoader).

## Example prompt

> A weathered lighthouse keeper standing on a cliff at golden hour, wind tugging at his oilskin coat, dramatic clouds behind him, cinematic lighting, highly detailed.

wan.raw:
# wan — prompting & settings guide

- **Prompting style:** natural_language
- **Negative prompt:** supported
- **Prompt weights** (e.g. `(word:1.2)`): not honored
- **Loader:** UNETLoader + CLIPLoader

## Recommended settings

| steps | cfg | sampler | scheduler | resolution |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 20 | 6 | uni_pc | simple | 832x480 |

## Tips

- Wan 2.x (text-to-video / image-to-video) takes natural-language descriptions of the scene AND its motion.
- It supports a negative prompt and real CFG (~5-7) — the bundled default negative trims artifacts and over-saturation.
- 480p (832x480) is the fast default; 720p costs significantly more time and memory.
- For image-to-video, resize/crop the reference image to the target resolution and aspect ratio (e.g. 832x480) before the I2V node — a mismatched reference gets stretched or cropped unexpectedly.

## Common mistakes

- Don't set cfg to 1.0 like a distilled model — full Wan checkpoints need cfg ~6; only the Lightning/distilled LoRAs run at low steps + cfg 1.
- Don't omit motion description — Wan needs verbs and camera direction to animate.
- Don't pass the reference image at its original resolution/aspect ratio into I2V without checking it against the target resolution first.

## Example prompt

> A paper boat drifting down a rain-soaked gutter, water rushing past, camera following low to the ground, reflections of city lights rippling on the surface.
